Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage across major business outlets is dominated by Anthropic's blockbuster IPO pricing and the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy, both seen as tests of the AI boom's durability. Geopolitical tension in the Strait of Hormuz and the ongoing US-Iran standoff are also driving oil markets, while Tuesday's US inflation report and a wave of corporate layoffs round out the agenda.

stories.headline: Anthropic sets IPO price range, targets up to $1.4 trillion valuation
stories.summary: Anthropic set a price range of $70-$78 a share for its Nasdaq debut, implying a valuation of up to roughly $1.4 trillion, down sharply from earlier $2 trillion talk, with trading expected to begin November 19.

stories.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang faces FBI scrutiny over alleged affair with Chinese spy
stories.summary: President Trump said the FBI is looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a woman identified as a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, intensifying questions about Nvidia's reliance on a single executive.

stories.headline: US and Iran trade strikes on islands for control of Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The US and Iran are engaged in a fierce battle over the strategic waterway, with strikes on islands in the strait rattling oil markets even as Trump downplayed the chance of further escalation.

stories.headline: China's trade surplus surges past $1 trillion in October
stories.summary: Chinese exports kept climbing despite domestic economic gloom and global trade tensions, pushing the annual trade surplus above the trillion-dollar mark.

stories.headline: SoftBank posts $7bn loss on US data centre writedown
stories.summary: The AI-focused Japanese group reported its first quarterly loss in nearly two years, blaming the hit on changing requirements tied to its US data center projects.

stories.headline: Markets await October CPI report as Fed's Waller backs a rate hike
stories.summary: A strong stock rebound stalled after Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he supports a December rate hike just ahead of Tuesday's closely watched inflation data.

stories.headline: Boeing and PepsiCo announce fresh layoffs as corporate cost-cutting spreads
stories.summary: Boeing said it will cut 5% of its commercial airplane workforce as 737 Max production ramps slower than planned, while PepsiCo separately said it will cut about 1,000 North American jobs amid sluggish home-market sales.

Business.gaps: Politico, Puck and The Economist had little distinctly business-relevant news in the window beyond what's cited above (Politico's feed skewed toward US midterm politics); Business Insider had no items in the provided feed or searchable results.

US politics.overview: Coverage across these outlets is dominated by the fallout from last week's Democratic midterm landslide: a looming House vote to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the Iran war, internal GOP turmoil over Senate and House leadership elections, and analysis of how Democrats' sweeping gains reshape the 2028 landscape. Secondary threads include Trump's shifting tone on immigration enforcement, a Supreme Court ruling on border wall construction, and economic ripple effects from the midterms like falling gas prices.

stories.headline: House poised to impeach Pete Hegseth after GOP midterm defeat
stories.summary: Axios reports House Republican leaders are bracing for enough GOP defections to impeach Defense Secretary Hegseth this week, as lawmakers who lost reelection have little left to lose and anger over the Iran war has eroded his support.

stories.headline: Senate GOP leadership elections proceed despite calls to delay
stories.summary: Senate Republicans are moving ahead with internal leadership elections for the new Congress even as a faction led by Sen. Ron Johnson pushes to delay them for a reckoning on the midterm losses.

stories.headline: House Republicans vote to elect a new leader after Johnson's exit
stories.summary: NPR reports House Republicans are voting Tuesday on a successor to Speaker Mike Johnson, who is stepping down, with Steve Scalise and Jim Jordan vying for the top minority leader post.

stories.headline: Democratic Party gained power nationwide in midterms — now what?
stories.summary: NPR examines how Democratic leaders across the country are now trying to figure out how to use the sweeping power voters handed them in the midterms.

stories.headline: A new set of Democratic power brokers just dropped before 2028
stories.summary: Politico reports presidential hopefuls are already working the phones to build relationships with a new slate of Democratic figures in key early states following the midterm wins.

stories.headline: Supreme Court allows Trump administration to continue border wall construction
stories.summary: SCOTUSblog reports the justices ruled a federal judge lacked authority to halt border wall construction, letting the Trump administration proceed.

stories.headline: Trump signals openness to softening immigration crackdown
stories.summary: RealClearPolitics describes Trump sending a notably softer message on allowing some illegal immigrants to stay, a shift from his previous hardline stance since retaking office.

stories.headline: Gas prices fall below $4 for first time since July
stories.summary: The Washington Post reports a sharp decline in pump prices followed election results signaling strong voter opposition to an extended war in Iran.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS and Cook Political Report had no new items in the last 24-48 hours in search results; coverage shown from them reflects older pre-election material only.

Tech & AI.overview: Tech and AI coverage over the last 48 hours is dominated by two intertwined mega-stories: the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy, and Anthropic's blockbuster IPO roadshow targeting a trillion-dollar-plus valuation. Secondary threads include new frontier model releases from Anthropic and Meta, AI security lapses (Claude Code leaking secrets, Hugging Face warning on open-source risks), and policy angles from Platformer and MIT Technology Review on how a newly Democratic Congress and data-center backlash could reshape AI regulation.

stories.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang scandal widens with Congressional summons and FBI scrutiny
stories.summary: The Information reports that leaders of three U.S. House committees have summoned Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to a closed-door briefing over his ties to Alice Huang, a Chinese executive reportedly identified as a spy, while Trump separately said the FBI is now investigating. TechCrunch and others add that Huang quietly hired a crisis PR firm with a history of handling sex scandals a year before the story broke, and the relationship allegedly facilitated over $7.5 billion in chip shipments to China since 2023.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches IPO roadshow targeting up to $1.4 trillion valuation
stories.summary: Anthropic announced it has launched its IPO roadshow, offering 825 million Class A shares priced between $70 and $78 each and planning to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. The filing could value the company at up to $1.4 trillion on a fully diluted basis, alongside a separate $26 billion round from cornerstone investors including Google, AMD and Nvidia, in what NYT calls one of the biggest public listings ever amid fears the AI boom isn't sustainable.

stories.headline: Anthropic ships Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 just ahead of IPO
stories.summary: Anthropic released its most powerful models yet, Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, in two tiers—one broadly available and one reserved for vetted organizations—timed just before its public listing. VentureBeat notes the release also cut API pricing by 20% while hitting record benchmark scores.

stories.headline: Claude Code's 'don't ask again' setting exposes thousands of secrets on GitHub
stories.summary: Researchers found that a convenience feature in Anthropic's Claude Code coding assistant has been inadvertently leaving passwords, API keys and other credentials exposed in public GitHub repositories. VentureBeat reports security firm Apiiro found 1,122 publicly accessible settings files containing real secrets across more than 100,000 examined repos, and Anthropic has acknowledged the issue without committing to a fix date.

stories.headline: Google DeepMind uses AI agents to formally verify Signal's encryption protocol
stories.summary: Google DeepMind researchers used an agentic AI framework called AlphaProof Code to verify the cryptographic guarantees underlying Signal's secure messaging protocol in a four-week proof-of-concept, according to Wired's Lily Hay Newman. The Register adds this combined human oversight with AI agents to check Signal's post-quantum handshake and Triple Ratchet mechanisms.

stories.headline: Chinese AI labs race to poach Silicon Valley talent, with limited success so far
stories.summary: Rest of World reports that Chinese AI startups like MiniMax and Moonshot are opening U.S. outposts to recruit top engineers, but steep pay gaps, lower prestige and national-security tensions are making it hard to lure talent away from OpenAI and Anthropic.

stories.headline: Data-center backlash and incoming AI regulation take shape after midterms
stories.summary: Casey Newton argues that a new Democratic majority in Congress has a mandate to rein in frontier AI labs and data centers but risks repeating mistakes from the failed push to regulate social media. MIT Technology Review separately reports that newly elected Rep. Scott Wiener, replacing Nancy Pelosi, is positioned to push AI regulation in Washington, while another MIT Tech Review piece suggests public anger over data centers is really about rising electricity costs.

stories.headline: Microsoft lobbies Trump administration against FCC ban on Chinese optical transceivers
stories.summary: Reuters reports via Techmeme that Microsoft is among a group of companies pressing the Trump administration to halt an FCC plan to ban imports of Chinese optical transceivers, a component used heavily in data center networking.

Tech & AI.gaps: The Verge, Wired, Ars Technica, NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist, The Guardian, and Google DeepMind's own blog could only be assessed via provided feed items or a limited search; some coverage from these outlets may exist beyond what was found.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate coverage this week is dominated by the fallout from the U.S. midterm elections, which saw a sweeping Democratic 'blue wave' built partly on voter anger over data centers and rising electricity bills, alongside the Senate's bipartisan permitting reform bill clearing a key procedural hurdle. A second major thread is Middle East oil market volatility tied to the Iran conflict and shifting Gulf supply dynamics, which is also feeding into projections of a rare dip in global fossil-fuel emissions.

stories.headline: Democrats' midterm sweep reshapes state and federal energy policy
stories.summary: Latitude Media reports that historic Democratic upsets in Texas, Ohio and Wisconsin, driven by anger over gasoline and electricity prices and data center buildouts, are poised to abruptly shift energy and data-center policy nationwide. Heatmap and Canary Media similarly described the results as opening the door to more ambitious clean-energy and affordability policies in newly flipped statehouses.

stories.headline: Senate permitting reform bill (BAAJA) survives first procedural vote
stories.summary: Heatmap reports that the Senate voted 73-25 to invoke cloture on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, a major permitting overhaul, even as Trump cast doubt on the deal hours later. Latitude Media separately detailed Democratic senators framing the bill as a direct response to affordability and data-center concerns raised by voters.

stories.headline: Voters deliver sweeping rebuke to data centers in dozens of ballot measures
stories.summary: Canary Media reports that Democrats who campaigned against data center expansion swept congressional and governors' races, with voters approving dozens of measures aimed at reining in the facilities. Latitude Media's analysis similarly found that a Jefferies note flagged "anything that touches data centers" as an election-night market loser.

stories.headline: Democrats flip Georgia's utility regulator for the first time in two decades
stories.summary: Heatmap reports that Democrats Peter Hubbard and Sheila Edwards won their races, securing a 3-2 Democratic majority on the Georgia Public Service Commission after a campaign focused on rising utility bills. Canary Media added that the new majority could push utility Georgia Power toward more rooftop solar, efficiency and clean energy for data-center demand.

stories.headline: Oil market starts pricing in a potential US-Iran deal
stories.summary: Bloomberg aired analyst commentary suggesting geopolitical risk premium from the Iran conflict has largely been erased from oil prices as a potential deal nears, while WSJ separately reported crude futures sliding after Trump downplayed further U.S. strikes on Iran.

stories.headline: Global fossil-fuel CO2 emissions projected to dip slightly in 2026
stories.summary: Carbon Brief's annual analysis projects fossil-fuel and cement CO2 emissions will fall roughly 0.4% in 2026 to about 38.2 billion tonnes, partly attributing the dip to reduced oil use linked to the Iran conflict.

stories.headline: Adnoc Gas still weighing ways to bypass the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: WSJ reports that Adnoc Gas's chief executive says the company has been examining alternatives to reduce its reliance on the Strait of Hormuz, including a possible LNG export facility on the UAE's east coast.

Energy.gaps: Argus Media could not be found via search in the allowed window; Reuters, FT, NYT and The Economist block web search and had no relevant feed items provided, so they are not represented here.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage across outlets is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admitted affair with a woman US officials suspect of Chinese espionage ties, which state media, Asian outlets and Western papers are all covering from different angles, alongside China's October trade data showing the annual surplus has again topped $1 trillion. Business and tech outlets are also tracking a reshaping auto/EV landscape (VW's China strategy reversal, BYD's export lead) and continued US-China tech-restriction maneuvering, while Hong Kong and Macau national-security prosecutions keep generating cross-border diplomatic friction.

stories.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair fuels 'Chinese spy' firestorm
stories.summary: State-run Global Times ran a series of pieces defending Huang and accusing US media and lawmakers of weaponizing unproven 'Chinese spy' claims against the Nvidia CEO for political and protectionist ends, while China's foreign ministry dismissed the allegations as a groundless smear. The controversy triggered a board investigation at Nvidia, a stock selloff, and calls from US lawmakers for tougher export controls on AI chips to China.

stories.headline: China's trade surplus tops $1 trillion for the year
stories.summary: China's October exports rose 35.2% year-on-year while imports jumped 41.6%, pushing the cumulative 2026 trade surplus past $1 trillion despite a strengthening yuan and growing Western scrutiny of the imbalance. Analysts noted AI-chip demand and EV exports are driving the surplus, while imports were lifted by higher energy and commodity prices rather than a genuine domestic demand recovery.

stories.headline: US lawmakers push tougher China export controls amid Nvidia scrutiny
stories.summary: Momentum is building in the newly Democrat-controlled Congress to attach a slate of stricter China export-control measures to the annual defense bill, with the Nvidia spy controversy adding political fuel. Nikkei Asia separately reported Washington extended a suspension of expanded blacklist rules on Chinese firms to January 10, prolonging the trade truce even as scrutiny intensifies.

stories.headline: Volkswagen overhauls 'In China, For China' strategy
stories.summary: Volkswagen is revising its localized China strategy as the German automaker struggles with a sharp sales downturn in the world's largest car market.

stories.headline: Macau jails pro-democracy ex-lawmaker Au Kam-san for 12.5 years
stories.summary: The US said it strongly condemns the sentencing of former Macau lawmaker and pro-democracy activist Au Kam San, the territory's first national-security conviction of this kind, with his wife calling the verdict a political judgment. The case adds to a wave of national-security prosecutions across Hong Kong and Macau, including the recent 10-year sentence given to activist Joshua Wong.

stories.headline: Chinese AI labs struggle to poach Silicon Valley talent
stories.summary: Chinese AI startups like MiniMax and Moonshot are opening US outposts to recruit top engineers, but face steep pay gaps, lower prestige, and national-security tensions that make luring talent from OpenAI and Anthropic difficult.

stories.headline: BYD retains lead in China's NEV exports as Tesla's share rises
stories.summary: BYD exported 164,679 new-energy vehicles in October, holding the top spot with a 28.3% export share even as its total fell from September, while Tesla's export share climbed to 10.1%. A companion report showed Tesla dropping out of the domestic retail top 10 as Xiaomi, Xpeng and Great Wall gained ground.

China.gaps: No recent coverage found for Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Yicai Global, CGTN, China Daily, or Xinhua in the search results; Reuters, AP, and NYT could not be searched directly and no relevant feed items from them were provided.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Gulf and Middle East outlets are dominated by the fallout of the prolonged US-Iran war: Houthi missile barrages on Saudi Arabia, continued US-Iran clashes near the Strait of Hormuz, and economic ripple effects across the Gulf. Israeli outlets are consumed by the swearing-in of the new Knesset and Gadi Eisenkot's push to form a government after Netanyahu lost his majority, while Gulf business press tracks oil-market shifts and AI investment risk tied to the conflict.

stories.headline: Missiles intercepted over Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks prompt emergency measures
stories.summary: Saudi air defenses intercepted missiles fired toward Riyadh and the kingdom's south for a third straight day, forcing Riyadh schools back to online classes, as Houthis say the strikes are retaliation for Saudi-led strikes that killed dozens in Sanaa over the weekend.

stories.headline: U.S., Iran Exchange Strikes on Islands as They Fight for Control of Strait
stories.summary: The US and Iran are trading strikes on islands in the Strait of Hormuz as both sides vie for control of the critical waterway, even as the Pentagon also moved refueling tankers out of a second UK base over an Iranian threat.

stories.headline: UAE Cuts Flagship Oil Price as Mideast Supply Jump Stirs Rivalry
stories.summary: The UAE slashed its flagship crude price premium for December supplies shortly after Saudi Arabia made similar cuts, as rebounding Middle East oil output intensifies competition; separately, analysts say oil markets are starting to price in a potential US-Iran deal.

stories.headline: Israel's 26th Knesset holds swearing-in ceremony as Eisenkot's bloc moves to assert control
stories.summary: Israel's new parliament was sworn in with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc now in the minority, as rival Gadi Eisenkot's bloc swiftly agreed on a new Knesset speaker and committee chairs while working to assemble a coalition.

stories.headline: Europeans upbeat after Qatari PM update on US-Iran peace talks and Trump meeting
stories.summary: European officials expressed optimism after Qatar's prime minister briefed them on his meeting with Donald Trump and joined G7 counterparts and Saudi Arabia's foreign minister in Paris to discuss efforts to end the Iran war.

stories.headline: Why the GCC is setting up an advanced military command base in Kuwait
stories.summary: Gulf Cooperation Council leaders agreed to establish a joint advanced military command headquarters in Kuwait, citing the need to strengthen defense coordination amid the region's prolonged conflict with Iran.

stories.headline: US midterm backlash puts Gulf AI dreams to the test
stories.summary: The Democrats' sweeping US midterm win raises new questions for Gulf states' multibillion-dollar AI partnerships with Washington, as tighter chip export controls and a Silicon Valley backlash threaten to complicate Saudi and Emirati ambitions to become global computing hubs.

stories.headline: UAE plans up to $55bn in energy infrastructure investment

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not find recent distinct coverage from Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English, The New Arab, Iran International or Zawya via search. Reuters, AP, FT, BBC and The Economist block web search and had no relevant items in the provided feed beyond what is reflected via Al-Monitor's Reuters-sourced wire pieces.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Pan-African outlets are converging on security and humanitarian crises — a DRC military court handing down mass death sentences, tens of thousands of Ethiopians fleeing into Kenya, and migrant boat disasters off Senegal and Greece — alongside geopolitical fallout from Russia's Africa summit and Sahel tensions. Business coverage centers on Nigerian banking and energy deals (Access Bank's subsidiary sell-offs, Dangote's refinery IPO) and investor sentiment toward African mining.

stories.headline: DR Congo sentences 66 soldiers to death for fleeing rebel fighting
stories.summary: A military court in the DRC handed down death sentences to 66 soldiers for desertion, mutiny and disobeying orders during fighting with rebel groups in the east.

stories.headline: Up to 50,000 Ethiopians flee to Kenya as clashes escalate
stories.summary: Escalating clashes inside Ethiopia since late October have pushed tens of thousands of refugees across the border into Kenya, prompting close UNHCR monitoring.

stories.headline: Niger and Chad's drone-strike row exposes deep rifts in the Sahel
stories.summary: A dispute over a drone strike has highlighted clashing alliances in the Sahel over France, Russia and rebel groups, despite diplomatic smiles at Moscow's summit and Algerian mediation efforts.

stories.headline: Putin's Africa summit delivered the spectacle, but what's really on the table?
stories.summary: Nearly half of Africa's leaders attended the third Russia-Africa summit in Moscow chasing deals on arms, nuclear power and education, though actual trade and investment remain limited. Africa Confidential separately reported that Moscow's summit failed to allay concerns over African recruits fighting for Russian forces in Ukraine.

stories.headline: Access Bank aims to sell up to 25% stakes in African subsidiaries
stories.summary: After years of rapid expansion, Access Bank plans to sell minority stakes in most of its African subsidiaries to local investors as it pivots from scale to value creation; TechCabal's daily briefing flagged the move as 'Access weighs foreign market exit.'

stories.headline: Dangote refinery's $1.6 billion IPO draws nearly triple demand
stories.summary: Nigerian investors placed roughly $4.78 billion in orders for Dangote's refinery share sale as the company prepares for a planned November listing, according to Africa Confidential's latest issue.

stories.headline: Senegalese families mourn sons lost in deadly migrant boat disaster
stories.summary: Grieving families in northeastern Senegal are coming to terms with the loss of loved ones after a migrant boat capsized off the coast, killing dozens; separate footage showed wreckage from a sinking that killed at least 39 people.

stories.headline: African mining seen poised for growth, but bankability risks need urgent action
stories.summary: Standard Bank's mining and metals executive Sean Evans said African mining is set to draw increased investment over the next three to five years on the back of geopolitical shifts and critical-minerals demand, but a shortage of new projects and weak infrastructure remain key constraints.

Africa.gaps: The Continent and African Business had no stories specific to the last 24-48 hours in search results (only older weekly issues/archives surfaced). Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block web search and no feed items from them were supplied for this group, so their current Africa coverage could not be assessed.

Media.overview: Media coverage over the past 48 hours is dominated by Trump's first post-midterm sit-down interview on '60 Minutes,' which multiple outlets say delivered unusually pointed questioning about his finances, alongside a blockbuster UK press-freedom story as The Guardian and ITV News finally named David Walliams after he lost his injunction bid. Trade outlets are also tracking the fallout from Skydance's CBS/CNN buyouts, the GOP's midterm drubbing reshaping scrutiny of media moguls who had courted Trump, and ongoing structural pressures on local journalism funding.

stories.headline: Ross Douthat presses Trump on $3 billion net worth and crypto ties in first post-midterm '60 Minutes' interview
stories.summary: In his first sit-down since the midterm losses, Trump was repeatedly pressed by new CBS correspondent Ross Douthat on his family's World Liberty Financial crypto company and foreign investment ties, with Trump insisting he knows nothing about the business run by his sons.

stories.headline: David Walliams named as the UK celebrity accused of grooming and sexual assault after losing injunction fight
stories.summary: Walliams was unmasked by a three-year joint Guardian/ITN investigation after failing to get a High Court injunction, with multiple women accusing him of grooming and assault involving girls as young as 15; he denies the allegations.

stories.headline: CJR questions what's next for outlets that capitulated to Trump after GOP's midterm rebuke
stories.summary: CJR argues media moguls overestimated Trump's political mandate and political support, raising questions about what comes next for outlets, including CBS and Paramount, that bent to pressure.

stories.headline: Skydance buyouts at CNN and CBS News spark staff exodus ahead of looming cuts
stories.summary: Status reports that Skydance's buyout offers at CNN and CBS News are driving veteran staffers to leave ahead of anticipated layoffs, with unintended consequences for the newsrooms.

stories.headline: What could the Times buy with its A.I. settlement money?
stories.summary: Puck's Dylan Byers writes that the New York Times' copyright lawsuit against Microsoft and OpenAI could soon yield a settlement of more than a billion dollars, potentially fueling a new M&A push by the paper's leadership.

stories.headline: Canada renews Local Journalism Initiative and extends journalism tax credit
stories.summary: Canada's proposed federal budget extends the journalism tax credit by hundreds of millions of dollars and expands eligibility to audio and audiovisual news, a lifeline for struggling local outlets.

stories.headline: Jemima Goldsmith accuses Russell Brand of 'violence, coercive control and abuse' after his rape sentencing
stories.summary: Producer Jemima Goldsmith said she was a victim of Brand's abuse during their relationship over a decade ago, speaking out after his recent 10-year prison sentence for rape and sexual assault.

stories.headline: Pentagon warns reporters who 'get out of line' will be removed from Hegseth press conference
stories.summary: Pentagon officials reportedly told reporters that anyone who acts 'silly' or steps out of line risks ejection from Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's upcoming news conference, renewing press-access tensions.

Media.gaps: No recent coverage could be independently verified via search for NYT, WSJ, FT, or The Guardian beyond their feed items provided (which were unrelated to media-industry topics), so only those feed items were used for those outlets.
